title: “It Feels Like Something Out of Science Fiction”: Astronomers Find First Green Star - Nautilus
gist: A University of Warwick study finds white dwarfs come in a range of colors, including the first green star, because color is not set by temperature alone for all of them.

insights.claim: A University of Warwick study finds white dwarfs come in a rainbow of colors rather than all being white.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Overturns a simple assumption about stellar remnants.
insights.locator: white dwarfs actually come in a rainbow of different colors

insights.claim: Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like perfect radiators whose color is set almost entirely by temperature, but little research had examined other possibilities for white dwarfs.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Departures from the perfect-radiator model point to unexplored astrophysics.
insights.quote: Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like ‘perfect radiators,’ so their color is set almost entirely by temperature
insights.locator: The color of most stars is a function
